scopeNote: Provisional coverage-driven decisions spanning suspicion, diagnostic criteria, imaging, culture-negative disease, pathogen treatment, selected transition strategies, surgery, embolic complications, devices and prevention. Not official examination weights.

checked: Stable suspected-case collection: at least three pre-antibiotic sets at roughly thirty-minute intervals.
TTE/TEE selection and repeat assessment depend on suspicion and anatomy.
Persistent bacteremia requires treatment and source reassessment; seventy-two hours does not automatically equal a formal surgical-persistence threshold.

sourceChecks.source: Duke–ISCVID 2023 criteria and AHA 2025 BCNE statement
checked: Formal Duke culture-count criteria differ from recommended sampling practice.
Diagnostic revision removes older complex timing/separate-venipuncture requirements; adequate aseptic collection remains necessary.
Prior antibiotic exposure is a major reason for culture-negative disease.
Current 2026 guidance, rather than relying on the older 2021 document, checked for prompt cultures and immediate antibiotics ideally within one hour in probable/definite sepsis or septic shock.
Stable IE collection spacing must not become an untreated delay in shock.

checks: Clinical definite: two major, one major plus three minor, or five minor; possible minimum combinations distinct from definite.
Repeated cultures do not multiply a microbiological major category; fever, predisposition and vascular phenomena are distinct minor domains.
sourceChecks.reviewStatus: Source checked during drafting; complete generated-chapter editorial review pending

sourceChecks.source: Duke–ISCVID 2023 primary criteria and ESC 2023 diagnostic guidance
checks: E. faecalis typical independently of source; additional typical pathogens with prosthetic material; blood molecular and method-specific serological major criteria.
Early prosthetic FDG uptake classification differs between the named frameworks; direct surgical observation is a conditional clinical major criterion, distinct from pathological confirmation.
TTE/TEE sequence, repeat imaging after five to seven days if suspicion remains high, and CT for inconclusive periannular anatomy; PET limitations and extracardiac assessment.
sourceChecks.reviewStatus: Source checked during drafting; full generated clinical editorial review pending

sourceChecks.source: AHA 2025 BCNE scientific statement and primary Whipple clinical series
checks: Distinguish pretreated ordinary pathogens from untreated nonroutine pathogens.
Expand directed investigation after approximately 72 hours of negative cultures; select tests by epidemiology and clinical setting.
Coxiella, Bartonella and Whipple diagnostic clues; complementary operative tissue investigations and cautious molecular interpretation.
sourceChecks.accessNote: AHA full-text and PDF direct opens encountered recaptcha/403; official AHA summary and indexed primary-statement passages were accessible. No claim of unrestricted full-text access.
sourceChecks.reviewStatus: Draft source checks; final complete-chapter review pending

sourceChecks.source: CDC current Q fever clinical guidance
checks: Adults with endocarditis or vascular infection: doxycycline 100 mg every 12 hours plus hydroxychloroquine 200 mg every 8 hours for at least 18 months; individualize with response.

sourceChecks.source: ESC 2023 antimicrobial, surgery, complication, device and prevention guidance; AHA 2015 legacy regimen cross-checks
sourceChecks.scope: Original questions 24–60, before insertion of five 2026-update questions
checks: Streptococcal full and restricted short courses; MSSA beta-lactams; enterococcal synergy and resistant-species distinction; HACEK valve-specific duration.
ESC-specific rifampin timing, bacterial course counting and new replacement prosthesis during NVE treatment.
Emergency versus urgent surgery, embolic indications and ischemic versus hemorrhagic neurological timing.
Splenic and renal complications, antithrombotic distinction, complete infected-system extraction and vegetation-specific reimplantation intervals.

sourceChecks.source: Vancomycin consensus, fungal guidance and primary trials
checks: AUC24 400–600 mg*h/L with MIC 1 mg/L.
Candida induction and early source control; at least six weeks postoperative antifungal treatment.
POET selected stable population and exclusions; EASE early embolic composite benefit without isolated mortality overstatement.

sourceChecks.source: AHA 2026 scientific statement, society-hosted primary full PDF and official current summary
checks: Added current consensus questions on penicillin-intermediate but ceftriaxone-susceptible streptococcal monotherapy and avoiding gentamicin in staphylococcal PVE; rifampin consensus remains unresolved.
Added postoperative-duration question: preoperative credit and at least fourteen postoperative days, without automatic clock reset for valve-test positivity alone; explicitly distinguished ESC 2023.
Added selected long-acting completion strategy and right-sided mechanical-aspiration evidence boundaries.
Added E. faecalis IE colonoscopy discussion; 2026 statement still identifies Duke–ISCVID 2023 as the contemporary diagnostic framework.
sourceChecks.limitation: Society-hosted PDF is the September 8 version. October 12 correction notice identified but not yet retrieved in full; final installation remains pending this check.

sourceChecks.source: DOTS randomized trial and 2026 AHA mechanical-aspiration advisory
checks: DOTS completion after clearance; 1500 mg days one/eight with renal adjustment as specified; left-sided IE and retained infected prosthesis excluded; primary superiority not established.
Aspiration selected for refractory or high-operative-risk right-sided cases, alongside antibiotics; no randomized efficacy/safety evidence.

sourceChecks.source: AHA dental prevention, NIH Bartonella dose check and BCNE primary statement
checks: Adult dental dose and timing, allergy alternatives, no clindamycin, high-risk cardiac/procedure intersection; AHA versus ESC nondental difference.
Bartonella doxycycline and rifampin doses checked with population-specific duration caution; ESC versus AHA Whipple treatment approaches explicitly distinguished.
Read ESC correction notices: relevant antibiotic tables changed; adult ampicillin dose cross-checked separately, and affected pediatric or amoxicillin-IV schedules are not quoted in this chapter.
Duke erratum corrects Streptococcus naming in exclusions, not the criteria combinations.
BCNE erratum concerns byline credentials rather than the therapeutic statements.
Fever-exclusion paper is a retrospective diagnostic reassessment; not used as an official replacement for named 2023 criteria.

editorialReviewProgress.reviewMethod: Original sixty generated stems, all options, keys and full explanations read in batches; five inserted update questions read in full afterward; revised diagnostic table and other affected content reread.
revisions: Replaced weak or unrelated distractors in bacteremia, imaging, molecular testing, culture-negative workup, rifampin timing, surgery, device and prophylaxis questions.
Expanded all diagnostic domains in the Duke table and highlighted gram doses and serological thresholds.
Removed potential short-course ambiguity by comparing individual agents and naming the ESC framework.
Corrected EASE endpoint timing and separated current AHA postoperative consensus from ESC 2023.
editorialReviewProgress.remaining: Retrieve and assess the October 2026 AHA correction, then finalize, install, audit, commit and push Chapter 10.
